claim: Motor-skill learning can be accompanied by both increases and decreases in brain activity.
source_text: Motor-skill learning can be accompanied by both increases and decreases in brain activity.
evidence_reasoning: This statement references established findings in the field, supported by citations to review papers (Dayan and Cohen, 2011; Penhune and Steele, 2012; Hardwick et al., 2013).

claim: Increases in brain activity during motor learning may indicate neural recruitment.
source_text: Increases may indicate neural recruitment
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of activity increases supported by citations to prior work (Grafton et al., 1995; Karni et al., 1995; Hazeltine et al., 1997; Floyer-Lea and Matthews, 2005; Lehericy et al., 2005; Penhune and Doyon, 2002; Penhune and Doyon, 2005).

claim: Decreases in brain activity during motor learning may imply that a region became unimportant or developed a more efficient representation of the skill.
source_text: while decreases may imply that a region became unimportant or developed a more efficient representation of the skill
evidence_reasoning: This interpretation is supported by citations to prior studies (Jenkins et al., 1994; Toni et al., 1998; Ungerleider et al., 2002; Poldrack et al., 2005; Xiong et al., 2009; Ma et al., 2010; Penhune and Doyon, 2005).

claim: Motor-skill acquisition is associated with the emergence of highly distinguishable activity patterns for trained movement sequences, in the absence of average activity increases.
source_text: Here we show that motor-skill acquisition is associated with the emergence of highly distinguishable activity patterns for trained movement sequences, in the absence of average activity increases.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main finding of the study, supported by experimental fMRI data and multivariate pattern analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Both untrained and trained sequences could be discriminated in primary and secondary motor areas using multivariate pattern analysis.
source_text: Using multivariate pattern analysis, both untrained and trained sequences could be discriminated in primary and secondary motor areas.
evidence_reasoning: This finding is directly supported by the classification analysis results presented in the study.

claim: Trained sequences were classified more reliably than untrained sequences, especially in the supplementary motor area.
source_text: However, trained sequences were classified more reliably, especially in the supplementary motor area.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct result from the multivariate pattern analysis comparing trained and untrained sequences.

claim: Skill learning leads to the development of specialized neuronal circuits which allow the execution of fast and accurate sequential movements without average increases in brain activity.
source_text: Our results indicate skill learning leads to the development of specialized neuronal circuits, which allow the execution of fast and accurate sequential movements without average increases in brain activity.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the combination of behavioral improvements, increased pattern discriminability, and absence of average activity increases observed in the data.

claim: Motor skill acquisition may lead to increased neural recruitment for trained behaviors, thereby increasing average activation.
source_text: On the one hand, motor skill acquisition may lead to increased neural recruitment for trained behaviors, thereby increasing average activation
evidence_reasoning: This hypothesis is supported by citations to multiple prior studies (Grafton et al., 1995; Karni et al., 1995; Hazeltine et al., 1997; Floyer-Lea and Matthews, 2005; Lehericy et al., 2005; Penhune and Doyon, 2002; Penhune and Doyon, 2005).

claim: Learning may result in the development of representations that produce the same behavior with higher neural efficiency, thereby reducing activity.
source_text: Alternatively, learning may result in the development of representations that produce the same behavior with higher neural efficiency, thereby reducing activity
evidence_reasoning: This alternative hypothesis is supported by citations to prior research (Jenkins et al., 1994; Toni et al., 1998; Ungerleider et al., 2002; Poldrack et al., 2005; Xiong et al., 2009; Ma et al., 2010; Penhune and Doyon, 2005).

claim: Motor practice may induce simultaneous signal increases due to increased neural recruitment and signal decreases due to more efficient encoding.
source_text: Finally, motor practice may induce simultaneous signal increases (due to increased neural recruitment) and signal decreases (due to more efficient encoding), making motor learning difficult to detect using traditional fMRI paradigms
evidence_reasoning: This hypothesis is supported by citation to Steele and Penhune, 2010, and represents an inference about the complexity of learning-related changes.

claim: The learning of fast motor sequences causes the development of more distinct cortical activation patterns associated with each individual sequence, independent of average activity changes.
source_text: Here we test the idea that the learning of fast motor sequences, a commonly-used task in the study of skill learning, causes the development of more distinct cortical activation patterns associated with each individual sequence, independent of average activity changes.
evidence_reasoning: This is the central hypothesis tested and supported by the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Supplementary motor area (SMA) is sensitive to sequential context, with individual neurons preferentially active for transitions between specific movements.
source_text: Single cell recording studies have demonstrated that supplementary motor area (SMA; Tanji and Shima, 1994) and primary motor cortex (M1; Matsuzaka et al., 2007) are sensitive to the sequential context and that individual neurons are preferentially active for transitions between specific movements.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by citations to single-cell recording studies (Tanji and Shima, 1994; Matsuzaka et al., 2007).

claim: Primary motor cortex (M1) is sensitive to sequential context, with individual neurons preferentially active for transitions between specific movements.
source_text: Single cell recording studies have demonstrated that supplementary motor area (SMA; Tanji and Shima, 1994) and primary motor cortex (M1; Matsuzaka et al., 2007) are sensitive to the sequential context and that individual neurons are preferentially active for transitions between specific movements.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by citation to single-cell recording study (Matsuzaka et al., 2007).

claim: The development of neuronal populations with training is thought to underlie the faster production of trained sequences.
source_text: The development of such neuronal populations with training is thought to underlie the faster production of trained sequences (Matsuzaka et al., 2007).
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation from prior work (Matsuzaka et al., 2007) about the functional significance of neuronal population changes.

claim: After prolonged training, some neurons code for longer fragments, firing preferentially at the beginning of specific sequences.
source_text: After prolonged training, some neurons even appear to code for longer fragments, firing preferentially at the beginning of specific sequences (Tanji and Shima, 1994).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by citation to single-cell recording study (Tanji and Shima, 1994).

claim: Trained sequences should be associated with the activation of more distinct neuronal populations than comparable untrained sequences.
source_text: This idea therefore predicts that trained sequence should be associated with the activation of more distinct neuronal populations than comparable untrained sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical prediction derived from the theoretical framework about neuronal specialization with training.

claim: Multi-voxel pattern analysis (MVPA) detects differences in voxel-by-voxel activity patterns in an area of cortex, even if these patterns are highly overlapping and defined by neuronal differences on a small spatial scale.
source_text: We tested this idea using 'multi-voxel pattern analysis' (MVPA), which detects differences in voxel-by-voxel activity patterns in an area of cortex, even if these patterns are highly overlapping and defined by neuronal differences on a small spatial scale
evidence_reasoning: This describes the established capabilities of MVPA, supported by citations (Kamitani and Tong, 2005; Swisher et al., 2010; Freeman et al., 2011).

claim: Participants were trained for 4 days to produce four different movement sequences with their left hand.
source_text: Participants were trained for 4 days to produce four different movement sequences with their left hand.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct description of the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: After training, participants underwent two fMRI scans, performing either four trained or four untrained sequences.
source_text: After training, participants underwent two fMRI scans, performing either four trained or four untrained sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental design of the scanning sessions.

claim: Initially, participants executed the sequences slowly and deliberately with pauses between individual presses.
source_text: Initially, participants executed the sequences slowly and deliberately with pauses between individual presses
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the behavioral data collected during the study.

claim: After training, the same sequence is produced much faster, with individual finger presses overlapping.
source_text: After training, the same sequence is produced much faster, with individual finger presses overlapping.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from the behavioral data comparing pre- and post-training performance.

claim: Left-hand movement times were 237 ms faster for trained than for untrained sequences.
source_text: the left-hand MTs were 237 ms (SE: ±42 ms) faster for trained than for untrained sequences
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the behavioral measurements.

claim: The difference in movement time between trained and untrained sequences was highly significant when correcting for small differences at pre-test, t(14) = 5.749, p<0.0001.
source_text: This difference was highly significant, also when correcting for small difference between the sequences at pre-test, t(14) = 5.749, p<0.0001.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from the analysis of behavioral data.

claim: Movement times for the untrained sequences dropped by 796 ms compared to pre-test, t(15) = 8.23, p<0.001.
source_text: MTs for the untrained sequences dropped by 796 ms (±97 ms) compared to pre-test, t(15) = 8.23, p<0.001
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the behavioral measurements showing general learning effects.

claim: A considerable part of the acquired skill was general, transferring to untrained sequences.
source_text: suggesting that a considerable part of the acquired skill was general
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the significant improvement in untrained sequences at post-test.

claim: Participants may have become faster at movement transitions between specific finger pairs, which would also enhance the production of untrained sequences.
source_text: For example, participants may have become faster at movement transitions between specific finger pairs. This ability would also enhance the production of untrained sequences
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for the observed general learning effects.

claim: Untrained sequences shared 59.6% of digit transitions with the trained sequences.
source_text: which shared 59.6% of digit transitions with the trained sequences
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measure of the overlap between trained and untrained sequences.

claim: The comparison of neural representations of trained and untrained sequences after learning will reveal correlates of the sequence-specific rather than general skill acquired during learning.
source_text: Therefore, the comparison of neural representations of trained and untrained sequences after learning will reveal correlates of the sequence-specific rather than general skill acquired during learning.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about what the neural comparison will reveal, given the behavioral results.

claim: The right hand showed a pre- to post-test drop of 570 ms for untrained sequences, t(15) = −7.13, p<0.001.
source_text: The right hand showed a pre- to post-test drop of 570 ms (±80 ms) for untrained sequences, t(15) = −7.13, p<0.001
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the behavioral measurements of the untrained hand.

claim: The right hand showed a sequence-specific advantage of 95 ms, significant after correcting for pre-test differences, t(14) = 2.802, p=0.014.
source_text: but also a sequence-specific advantage of 95 ms (±31.45 ms), again significant after correcting for pre-test differences, t(14) = 2.802, p=0.014
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result showing intermanual transfer of sequence-specific learning.

claim: Participants acquired a sequence-specific skill representation that also enhanced performance of the untrained hand.
source_text: Thus, participants acquired a sequence-specific skill representation that also enhanced performance of the untrained hand.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the behavioral data showing intermanual transfer.

claim: Trained sequences were not associated with more activity than untrained sequences.
source_text: Despite these faster and harder presses, trained sequences were not associated with more activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct result from the fMRI analysis comparing average activity levels.

claim: A direct contrast only revealed areas with less activity for trained vs untrained sequences.
source_text: Rather, a direct contrast only revealed areas with less activity for trained vs untrained sequences
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the statistical contrast of fMRI data.

claim: Lower activity for trained sequences was found in both hemispheres in PMd and in areas along the IPS.
source_text: Lower activity for trained sequences was found in both hemispheres in PMd and in areas along the IPS.
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific result from the fMRI analysis identifying regions with reduced activity.

claim: Signal decreases were more pronounced in the left than in the right hemisphere, t(15) = 2.689, p=0.017.
source_text: Interestingly, the signal decreases (averaged over all fronto-parietal motor regions) were more pronounced in the left than in the right hemisphere, t(15) = 2.689, p=0.017.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result comparing hemispheric differences in activity changes.

claim: No cortical or subcortical area showed significantly more activity during the production of the trained compared to untrained sequences.
source_text: No cortical or subcortical area (the cerebellum was not covered) showed significantly more activity during the production of the trained compared to untrained sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is a negative result from the whole-brain fMRI analysis.

claim: In regions involved in the production of motor sequences, individual movement sequences would be associated with distinct patterns of cortical activity.
source_text: We predicted that in regions involved in the production of motor sequences, individual movement sequences would be associated with distinct patterns of cortical activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is the central prediction of the study, based on theoretical considerations.

claim: Classification was best in right M1, bilaterally in PMd, and on the medial bank of the IPS, where group-averaged accuracies reached ∼55%.
source_text: Classification was best in right M1, bilaterally in PMd, and on the medial bank of the IPS, where group-averaged accuracies reached ∼55% (chance performance was 25%).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the multivariate pattern analysis.

claim: Significant classification was found in PMv, SMA, and pre-SMA, each of which was highly significant after correcting for multiple tests.
source_text: We also found significant classification in PMv, SMA, and pre-SMA, each of which was highly significant after correcting for multiple tests
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the statistical analysis of classification accuracies.

claim: Above-chance classification accuracy implies that different sequences were represented as distinct spatial activation patterns.
source_text: Does above-chance classification accuracy imply that different sequences were represented as distinct spatial activation patterns as hypothesized
evidence_reasoning: This is a question about the interpretation of classification results, addressed through further analysis.

claim: Classification accuracy in three ROIs does not improve when adding more than two temporal components.
source_text: Adding further temporal components does not improve classification accuracy.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the temporal component analysis of the BOLD response.

claim: Classification accuracy for S1 was already above chance for the second TR, which was acquired 2.7–5.4 s after the onset of the number cue, t(15) = 3.335, p=0.002.
source_text: First, classification accuracy for S1 was already above chance for the second TR, which was acquired 2.7–5.4 s after the onset of the number cue, t(15) = 3.335, p=0.002.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from the temporal analysis of classification accuracy.

claim: All other regions showed significant classification accuracy at the third TR, all t(15) > 5.34, p<0.0001.
source_text: All other regions showed significant classification accuracy at the third TR, all t(15) > 5.34, p<0.0001.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from the temporal analysis across multiple regions.

claim: It is likely that the informative patterns were caused at least partly by instruction-related activity.
source_text: Thus, it is likely that the informative patterns were caused at least partly by instruction-related activity.
evidence_reasoning: This inference is based on the timing of when classification accuracy became significant.

claim: Areas such as OPJ and PMd exhibited sustained classification accuracy over the whole trial.
source_text: Secondly, even areas such as OPJ and PMd exhibited sustained classification accuracy over the whole trial.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the temporal analysis of classification accuracy.

claim: These areas did not only represent the string of numbers presented on the screen; rather they exhibited a sustained representation of the sequence during the execution phase.
source_text: Thus, these areas did not only represent the string of numbers presented on the screen; rather they exhibited a sustained representation of the sequence during the execution phase, during which the number cue was not visible anymore.
evidence_reasoning: This interpretation is based on the sustained classification accuracy observed during execution.

claim: Each sequence would be associated with a unique spatial activation pattern.
source_text: Importantly, our hypothesis predicted that each sequence would be associated with a unique spatial activation pattern.
evidence_reasoning: This is the specific hypothesis being tested with the dimensionality analysis.

claim: All sequence representations showed the highest accuracy when using all three available linear components.
source_text: we found here that all sequence representations showed the highest accuracy when using all three available linear components
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the dimensionality analysis of spatial patterns.

claim: This was the case in all ROIs and for both untrained sequences (all t(15) > 2.496, p<0.025) and trained sequence (all t(15) > 5.261, p<0.001).
source_text: This was the case in all ROIs and for both untrained sequences (all t(15) > 2.496, p<0.025) and trained sequence (all t(15) > 5.261, p<0.001).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result confirming the dimensionality finding across regions and conditions.

claim: Sequences are encoded in unique spatial activation patterns, rather than in differently scaled versions of a single pattern.
source_text: Thus, we can conclude that sequences are encoded in unique spatial activation patterns, rather than in differently scaled versions of a single pattern.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the dimensionality analysis results.

claim: The distinctiveness of cortical activation patterns, measured by classification accuracy, should increase with training.
source_text: Our central prediction was that the distinctiveness of cortical activation patterns, measured by classification accuracy, should increase with training.
evidence_reasoning: This is the central prediction of the study based on the theoretical framework.

claim: For trained sequences, classification accuracy was on average significantly higher (38.4%, ±1.39%) than for untrained sequences (34.2%, ±1.76%), t(15) = 2.203, p=0.022.
source_text: For trained sequences, classification accuracy (Figure 3C, red/purple, Figure 3—figure supplement 1) reached 60%—and was on average significantly higher for trained (38.4%, ±1.39%) than for untrained sequences (34.2%, ±1.76%), t(15) = 2.203, p=0.022.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the comparison of classification accuracies.

claim: The cortical surface area which encoded the sequences better than chance increased from 35.12 cm2 to 46.93 cm2, t(15) = 1.963, p=0.034.
source_text: Furthermore, the cortical surface area which encoded the sequences better than chance (within subject threshold: acc > 37.5%, Z > 1.64), increased from 35.12 cm2 (±5.38 cm2) to 46.93 cm2 (±4.65 cm2), t(15) = 1.963, p=0.034.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result showing the spatial extent of sequence encoding.

claim: After correcting for multiple comparisons over the whole cortical surface, only the increase in left SMA/pre-SMA was significant (p-corrected < 0.012).
source_text: After correcting for multiple comparisons over the whole cortical surface, only the increase in left SMA/pre-SMA was significant (uncorrected threshold p=0.002, t(15) > 3.39; p-corrected < 0.012; clustersize = 0.19 cm2).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from the map-wise comparison of trained and untrained sequences.

claim: In left SMA/pre-SMA, the accuracy increased from 36% to 46%.
source_text: In this area, the accuracy increased from 36% to 46%
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result showing the magnitude of change in classification accuracy.

claim: Untrained sequences were associated with unique, but basically random activity patterns.
source_text: Our data indicates that untrained sequences were associated with unique, but basically random activity patterns.
evidence_reasoning: This interpretation is based on the dimensionality analysis comparing observed patterns to simulated random patterns.

claim: Practice should lead to the development of dedicated neuronal populations for trained sequence transitions, which would cause each sequence to activate a unique subset of the network.
source_text: For the trained sequences, we reasoned that practice should lead to the development of dedicated neuronal populations for trained sequence transitions. This development would cause each sequence to activate a unique subset of the network, that is reduce the overlap between patterns.
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical prediction about how training should affect neural representations.

claim: The activity patterns for trained sequences were more evenly distributed than expected for spatially random patterns.
source_text: While the observed classification accuracy curves for trained sequences did not fully reach this extreme prediction, the activity patterns were more evenly distributed than expected for spatially random patterns
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from comparing observed patterns to simulated distributions.

claim: The classification accuracy for the one-dimensional classifier deviated significantly from the prediction based on random patterns for S1, M1, PMd, SMA/pre-SMA, and IPS, all t(15) > 2.429, p<0.028.
source_text: The classification accuracy for the one-dimensional classifier deviated significantly from the prediction based on random patterns for S1, M1, PMd, SMA/pre-SMA, and IPS, all t(15) > 2.429, p<0.028.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from the dimensionality analysis across multiple regions.

claim: The individual differences in overall classification accuracy did not correlate with the difference in MT (p=0.75), force (p=0.51), or error rate (p=0.21).
source_text: Furthermore, we tested whether the increase in discriminability of cortical activation patterns could have been caused by the reduced behavioral variability that normally accompanies learning. In considering this idea, it is important to keep in mind that classification accuracy is determined both by within-sequence variability and by between-sequences differences. To evaluate both together, we tested how well a linear classifier could discriminate between each set of four sequences based on MT, average force, or error rate, either considered in isolation or in any combination as separate features. None of the seven combinations showed a significant difference between trained and untrained sequences (all t(15) < 1.15, p>0.269
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the control analysis testing whether behavioral differences could explain the neural findings.

claim: When including the differences in classification accuracy based on all behavioral variables as a covariate, the accuracy difference based on fMRI patterns remained significant, t(15) = 2.56, p=0.01.
source_text: Furthermore, when including the differences in classification accuracy based on all behavioral variables as a covariate, the accuracy difference based on fMRI patterns remained significant, t(15) = 2.56, p=0.01.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from the covariate analysis.

claim: The higher classification accuracy for trained sequences was not a simply a consequence of more stable behavioral performance.
source_text: Thus, the higher classification accuracy for trained sequences was not a simply a consequence of more stable behavioral performance.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is based on the control analyses showing no relationship between behavioral and neural classification differences.

claim: The sequence-specific component of the activity patterns increases in strength with training.
source_text: In summary, our study shows for the first time that the sequence-specific component of the activity patterns increases in strength with training.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main conclusion from the pattern decomposition analysis.

claim: The variance explained by the common pattern outstrips the variance associated with the sequence specific component by a factor of 100 or more.
source_text: The variance explained by the common pattern outstrips the variance associated with the sequence specific component by a factor of 100 or more.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the pattern decomposition analysis.

claim: The strength of the common component follows the mean activation, while the sequence-specific component shows the same advantage for the trained compared to the untrained sequences evident in the classification accuracy.
source_text: While the strength of the common component follows the mean activation (Figure 5), the sequence-specific component shows the same advantage for the trained compared to the untrained sequences evident in the classification accuracy.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the pattern decomposition analysis comparing common and sequence-specific components.

claim: Different sequences of the same five finger presses are associated with overlapping but discriminable patterns of activity.
source_text: Together, our results show that different sequences of the same five finger presses are associated with overlapping but discriminable patterns of activity
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary conclusion from the multivariate pattern analysis results.

claim: These differences in activity patterns are more pronounced when the specific sequences are trained for multiple days.
source_text: and that these differences are more pronounced when the specific sequences are trained for multiple days
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary conclusion from the comparison of trained and untrained sequences.

claim: The changes likely reflect the formation of specialized neuronal circuits that enable fast and accurate sequential movements.
source_text: The changes likely reflect the formation of specialized neuronal circuits that enable fast and accurate sequential movements.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the observed neural and behavioral changes.

claim: The differential activation patterns reflect, at least partly, populations of neurons with preferential tuning for the sequential context of movements.
source_text: We hypothesize that the differential activation patterns reflect, at least partly, populations of neurons with preferential tuning for the sequential context of movements.
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis about the neural basis of the observed patterns, informed by prior single-cell recording studies.

claim: Neurons in M1 and SMA and pre-SMA have been reported to be preferentially active during performance of specific movement transitions.
source_text: Neurons in M1 (Matsuzaka et al., 2007) and SMA and pre-SMA (Tanji and Shima, 1994) have been reported to be preferentially active during performance of specific movement transitions.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by citations to prior neurophysiology studies.

claim: Regions that contain neurons with sequential tuning will activate slightly different neuronal populations depending on movement order.
source_text: Regions that contain either type of neuron will therefore activate slightly different neuronal populations depending on movement order.
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the consequences of having sequentially-tuned neurons.

claim: To be visible in fMRI, the patterns of presynaptic input to these neuronal populations must differ on a relatively coarse spatial scale.
source_text: To be visible in fMRI, the patterns of presynaptic input to these neuronal populations must differ on a relatively coarse spatial scale.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the spatial resolution requirements for fMRI detection of neural patterns.

claim: MVPA is able to decode information that relies on fine-grained spatial details of activity patterns.
source_text: Although MVPA is able to decode information that relies on fine-grained spatial details of activity patterns (Swisher et al., 2010; Freeman et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This is an established capability of MVPA, supported by citations.

claim: It was not clear a priori that sequential tuning would be clustered enough to reveal such representations at standard fMRI resolution.
source_text: it was not clear a priori that sequential tuning would be clustered enough to reveal such representations at standard fMRI resolution
evidence_reasoning: This expresses uncertainty about whether the neural organization would be detectable with fMRI.

claim: A set of areas was found, highly replicable across subjects, with activity patterns that distinguished reliably between sequences.
source_text: However, we found a set of areas, highly replicable across subjects, with activity patterns that distinguished reliably between sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of the classification results showing consistent findings across participants.

claim: The ability to distinguish between untrained sequences may be related to the substantial generalization of learning to the untrained sequences.
source_text: This finding may be related to the substantial generalization of learning to the untrained sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for why untrained sequences could be classified.

claim: Classification may have relied on populations of neurons that encode for the sequential transitions between pairs of fingers.
source_text: For example, classification may have relied on populations of neurons that encode for the sequential transitions between pairs of fingers, many of which were shared between trained and untrained sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for the mechanism underlying classification of untrained sequences.

claim: The unique activity patterns for untrained sequences likely relied on preexisting neuronal coding of sequential context.
source_text: More likely, however, the unique activity patterns for untrained sequences relied on preexisting neuronal coding of sequential context
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation based on general knowledge about motor behavior.

claim: Humans engage in many sequential motor behaviors such as typing on a keyboard or playing an instrument.
source_text: whether typing on a keyboard or playing an instrument, humans engage in many sequential motor behaviors
evidence_reasoning: This is general knowledge about human motor behavior.

claim: General representations of sequential context would discriminate between trained and untrained sequences alike.
source_text: and such general representations would discriminate between trained and untrained sequences alike
evidence_reasoning: This is a logical inference about the consequences of having general sequential representations.

claim: Sequential representations were found in motor areas in which single-cell neurophysiology has revealed such encoding before (i.e., M1 and SMA).
source_text: We found sequential representations in motor areas in which single-cell neurophysiology has revealed such encoding before (i.e., M1 and SMA; Matsuzaka et al., 2007; Tanji and Shima, 1994)
evidence_reasoning: This connects the current findings to prior neurophysiology studies.

claim: Sequential representations were also found in a set of parietal and lateral premotor areas.
source_text: but also in a set of parietal and lateral premotor areas
evidence_reasoning: This is a novel finding from the current study.

claim: Other imaging studies have reported increased activity in some of these regions with increased sequential processing demands.
source_text: While other imaging studies have reported increased activity in some of these regions with increased sequential processing demands (Farooqui et al., 2012; Heim et al., 2012)
evidence_reasoning: This references prior imaging studies showing activity changes in similar regions.

claim: This study is the first to show that individual voxels are tuned for different sequence of movements.
source_text: our study is the first to show that individual voxels are tuned for different sequence of movements
evidence_reasoning: This claims novelty for the current findings.

claim: Sequential encoding is not unique to the SMA, but is rather widespread throughout the cortical motor hierarchy.
source_text: Together with other neurophysiological recording study (Fogassi et al., 2005), our results argue that sequential encoding is not unique to the SMA, but is rather widespread throughout the cortical motor hierarchy.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the current data combined with prior neurophysiology studies.

claim: Each area does not simply discriminate between sequences based on one single variable (difficulty, force, etc), but each sequence is associated with a unique activity pattern.
source_text: The dimensionality analysis (Figure 5) indicated that each of these areas does not simply discriminate between sequences based on one single variable (difficulty, force, etc), but that each sequence is associated with a unique activity pattern.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the dimensionality analysis.

claim: The exact response characteristics of the underlying neuronal populations remain unclear.
source_text: The exact response characteristics of the underlying neuronal populations remain unclear, however.
evidence_reasoning: This acknowledges limitations in interpreting the neural mechanisms.

claim: Some of these regions could represent the sequences phonologically as string of number during subvocal rehearsal.
source_text: Some of these regions could represent the sequences phonologically as string of number during subvocal rehearsal (Hartwigsen et al., 2013)
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative alternative explanation for the observed patterns.

claim: Neural populations could code for the order of finger presses or their relative timing.
source_text: Furthermore, neural populations could code for the order of finger presses or their relative timing (Kornysheva et al., 2013)
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative possibility about what neural populations might encode.

claim: Representations could be effector-specific or independent of hand that is used to execute the movement.
source_text: and representations could be effector-specific or independent of hand that is used to execute the movement (Gallivan et al., 2013)
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative possibility about the nature of the representations.

claim: The experimental design did not allow conclusive determination of to what degree sequential decoding relied only on activity related to the execution versus the instruction phase.
source_text: Our experimental design also did not allow us to determine conclusively to what degree sequential decoding relied only on activity related to the execution, or to what degree these patterns were also present during the instruction phase.
evidence_reasoning: This acknowledges a limitation of the experimental design.

claim: Further dedicated experiments are needed to identify the exact nature of the sequential representations in identified areas.
source_text: Further dedicated experiments are needed to identify the exact nature of the sequential representations in identified areas.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about future research needs.

claim: Training promotes the formation of specialized neural representations and hence leads to more distinguishable activity patterns.
source_text: Our main hypothesis, however, was that training promotes the formation of specialized neural representations and hence leads to more distinguishable activity patterns.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main hypothesis that was tested and supported by the data.

claim: Averaged across all involved areas, trained sequences were better classified than untrained sequences.
source_text: Indeed, averaged across all involved areas, we were better able to classify between trained than between untrained sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary result from the classification analysis.

claim: Training-related changes became most evident when looking at multiple spatial components of the activity patterns.
source_text: Furthermore, we could show that these training-related changes became most evident when looking at multiple spatial components of the activity patterns.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the dimensionality analysis.

claim: The changes in classification accuracy were not due to larger between-sequence differences, or lower within-sequence variability, of a single behavioral factor.
source_text: First, it shows that the changes in classification accuracy were not due to larger between-sequence differences, or lower within-sequence variability, of a single behavioral factor—otherwise the difference would have been apparent using a classifier that uses only the most informative spatial pattern component.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the dimensionality analysis ruling out alternative explanations.

claim: Training leads to the formation of a unique spatial activity pattern for each sequence and therefore a more even spacing of the activity patterns in the space of possible patterns.
source_text: Secondly, it shows that training leads to the formation of a unique spatial activity pattern for each sequence and therefore a more even spacing of the activity patterns in the space of possible patterns.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the dimensionality analysis about how training changes pattern structure.

claim: Learning was caused by the formation of specialized neuronal circuits that encodes different finger transitions or whole sequences.
source_text: This lends some credibility to the idea that learning caused by the formation of specialized neuronal circuits that encodes different finger transitions or whole sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the findings about the neural mechanism of learning.

claim: The largest difference in classification accuracies was observed in the left SMA and pre-SMA.
source_text: The largest (and in a whole-brain comparison most reliable) difference in classification accuracies was observed in the left SMA and pre-SMA.
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific result identifying the region with the strongest learning effect.

claim: The SMA/pre-SMA finding likely reflects neuronal circuits specialized for longer sequence segments, a representation that would be highly specific to the trained sequences.
source_text: This likely reflects neuronal circuits specialized for longer sequence segments, a representation that would be highly specific to the trained sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of why SMA/pre-SMA showed the largest effect.

claim: M1 showed good discrimination for the untrained sequences, possibly reflecting representations of shorter sequence elements.
source_text: Other areas, such as M1, also showed good discrimination for the untrained sequences, possibly reflecting representations of shorter sequence elements.
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation with a speculative interpretation about what M1 represents.

claim: In the framework of hierarchical sequence representations, sequence-specific units in SMA may trigger the shorter sequence elements in M1.
source_text: In the framework of hierarchical sequence representations (Kiebel et al., 2009), sequence-specific units in SMA may trigger the shorter sequence elements in M1.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative interpretation within a theoretical framework from prior work.

claim: A number of previous studies have highlighted the SMA and pre-SMA as critical structures for skillful production of motor sequences.
source_text: A number of previous studies have highlighted the SMA and pre-SMA as critical structures for skillful production of motor sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This references prior literature on the role of SMA/pre-SMA.

claim: Disruption of the mesial frontal cortex caused increased errors during performance of complex sequential finger movements.
source_text: Disruption of the mesial frontal cortex caused increased errors during performance of complex sequential finger movements (Gerloff et al., 1997)
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from a prior study cited to support the importance of SMA.

claim: Disruption of the mesial frontal cortex left performance of simple finger sequences unaltered.
source_text: while leaving performance of simple finger sequences unaltered
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the same prior study showing specificity of the effect.

claim: Pre-SMA stimulation caused slowing in the transition between different sequences.
source_text: A second study showed slowing in the transition between different sequences after pre-SMA stimulation (Kennerley et al., 2004).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from another prior study supporting the role of pre-SMA.

claim: In non-human primates, muscimol injections into SMA and pre-SMA lead to errors in memory-guided performance of arm movement sequences.
source_text: In non-human primates, muscimol injections into SMA and pre-SMA lead to errors in memory-guided performance of arm movement sequences (Shima and Tanji, 1998).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from a primate study supporting the role of SMA/pre-SMA.

claim: Although the left hand was trained and tested, learning-related changes were either bilateral or in some cases even more pronounced in the ipsilateral, left hemisphere.
source_text: Although we trained and tested the left hand, learning-related changes were either bilateral, especially in regions that appear to code for actions with both hand (Gallivan et al., 2013), or in some cases even more pronounced in the ipsilateral, left hemisphere.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result about the lateralization of learning effects.

claim: The finding of stronger effects in the left hemisphere is consistent with specialization of the left hemisphere for complex movements, executed with either the dominant or non-dominant hand.
source_text: The latter finding is consistent with specialization of the left hemisphere for complex movements, executed with either the dominant or non-dominant hand (Verstynen et al., 2005).
evidence_reasoning: This interpretation connects the current finding to prior work on hemispheric specialization.

claim: Behavioral measures indicate inter-manual transfer of the sequence-specific knowledge to the untrained right hand.
source_text: Indeed, our behavioral measures indicate inter-manual transfer of the sequence-specific knowledge to the untrained right hand.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the behavioral testing of the untrained hand.

claim: The increases in discriminability of cortical activation patterns contrasted drastically with changes in average activity.
source_text: The increases in discriminability of cortical activation patterns contrasted drastically with changes in average activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary comparison of the two types of analysis results.

claim: Generally, less activity was observed for trained than untrained sequences, despite the fact that the two conditions were matched for error rate and the trained sequences were executed slightly faster and with higher peak forces.
source_text: Generally, we observed less activity for trained than untrained sequences, despite the fact that the two conditions were matched for error rate (and hence difficulty) and the trained sequences were executed slightly faster and with higher peak forces.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from the average activity analysis.

claim: In areas that showed the largest increases in classification accuracy, no changes in average activation were found.
source_text: In areas that showed the largest increases in classification accuracy, no changes in average activation were found.
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific result showing dissociation between pattern and average activity changes.

claim: Average activity changes during learning are likely complicated by the overlap of two competing tendencies.
source_text: Average activity changes during learning are likely complicated by the overlap of two competing tendencies.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of why average activity changes are difficult to interpret.

claim: Training likely leads to increased recruitment of neuronal populations, as has been shown with expansion of the cortical hand area following skill training.
source_text: First, training likely leads to increased recruitment of neuronal populations, as has been shown with expansion of the cortical hand area following skill training (Nudo et al., 1996).
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation supported by citation to prior work on cortical reorganization.

claim: Involving larger populations of neurons in motor planning and execution may reduce neuronal noise and lead to less variable performance.
source_text: Involving larger populations of neurons in motor planning and execution may reduce neuronal noise and lead to less variable performance.
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical explanation for why increased recruitment might be beneficial.

claim: The recruited neurons likely become more specialized for specific trained behaviors, therefore fewer non-specialized units must be recruited, decreasing the activity for the majority of neurons in a region.
source_text: Second, the recruited neurons likely become more specialized for specific trained behaviors. Therefore, fewer non-specialized units must be recruited, decreasing the activity for the majority of neurons in a region (Poldrack, 2000).
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical explanation for activity decreases, supported by citation.

claim: The overlap of increased neuronal recruitment and increased efficiency through specialization may explain previously inconsistent results about activity changes during learning.
source_text: The overlap of increased neuronal recruitment and increased efficiency through specialization (Steele and Penhune, 2010) may explain previously inconsistent results, which suggest that activity in sequence-related regions increases (Grafton et al.,1995; Karni et al., 1995; Floyer-Lea and Matthews, 2005; Hazeltine et al., 1997), decreases (Wu et al., 2004; Poldrack et al., 2005), or changes non-linearly over the course of learning (Xiong et al., 2009; Ma et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation that attempts to reconcile conflicting findings in the literature.

claim: The representational analysis employed here directly reflects the increased specialization of cortical circuits for trained behaviors.
source_text: In contrast, the representational analysis employed here directly reflects the increased specialization of cortical circuits for trained behaviors.
evidence_reasoning: This is a claim about what the MVPA approach measures, based on the results.

claim: Although average activity decreased in most areas, increased bilateral encoding of the trained sequences was found.
source_text: Although average activity decreased in most areas, we found increased bilateral encoding of the trained sequences.
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of the contrasting findings from the two analysis approaches.

claim: Examining average activity alone, one might be tempted to conclude that many secondary motor areas play a reduced role in the production of highly trained skills.
source_text: Examining average activity alone, one might be tempted to conclude that many secondary motor areas play a reduced role in the production of highly trained skills, which may be encoded in a few execution-related areas such as the primary motor cortex (Penhune and Steele, 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is a potential misinterpretation that could arise from only examining average activity.

claim: Skill learning generates increasingly specialized representations, which are distributed widely across both primary and secondary cortical motor areas.
source_text: In contrast, our results indicate that skill learning generates increasingly specialized representations, which are distributed widely across both primary and secondary cortical motor areas.
evidence_reasoning: This is the main conclusion about the distributed nature of learning-related changes.

claim: Eight female and eight male healthy, right-handed volunteers (22.4 years, SD = 2.6), participated in the experiment.
source_text: Eight female and eight male healthy, right-handed volunteers (22.4 years, SD = 2.6), participated in the experiment.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the participant sample.

claim: The UCL Ethics Committee approved all study procedures.
source_text: The UCL Ethics Committee approved all study procedures.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about ethical approval for the study.

claim: An fMRI-compatible response box was used, equipped with five piano-like keys, each incorporating a sensor that continuously measured isometric forces during sequence production.
source_text: We used an fMRI-compatible response box, equipped with five piano-like keys, each incorporating a sensor (FSG-15N1A; Sensing & Control Honeywell Inc., Morristown, NJ) that continuously measured isometric forces during sequence production.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the experimental apparatus.

claim: Each sequence contained each of the five fingers once and differed only in their order.
source_text: Each sequence contained each of the five fingers once and differed only in their order.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the sequence design.

claim: None of the sequences contained an ascending or descending sub-sequence of more than three neighboring fingers.
source_text: None of the sequences contained an ascending or descending sub-sequence of more than three neighboring fingers.
evidence_reasoning: This is a constraint on the sequence design to control difficulty.

claim: Participants were instructed to decrease their MT if they had an error-rate of less than 20% and to focus on accuracy if the error rate was larger than 20%.
source_text: We instructed participants to decrease their MT if they had an error-rate of less than 20% and to focus on accuracy if the error rate was larger than 20%.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the speed-accuracy instructions given to participants.

claim: This speed-accuracy instruction served to keep error-rates stable across the experiment.
source_text: This speed-accuracy instruction served to keep error-rates stable across the experiment.
evidence_reasoning: This explains the purpose of the instruction protocol.

claim: Imaging data were acquired on a 3T Siemens Trio MRI scanner using a 32-channel head coil.
source_text: Imaging data were acquired on a 3T Siemens Trio MRI scanner using a 32-channel head coil.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the MRI scanner specifications.

claim: The imaging arrangement covered the dorsal part of both cerebral hemispheres, but not the inferior temporal lobe or the cerebellum.
source_text: This arrangement covered the dorsal part of both cerebral hemispheres, but not the inferior temporal lobe or the cerebellum.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the spatial coverage of the imaging protocol.

claim: To determine whether a specific area of cortex showed reliably different patterns of activity for the four tested sequences, 160 voxels contained within a spherical patch of cortex were sequentially selected and submitted to linear discriminant analysis.
source_text: To determine whether a specific area of cortex showed reliably different patterns of activity for the four tested sequences, we sequentially selected 160 voxels contained within a spherical patch of cortex (see surface-based searchlight below) and then submitted these to a linear discriminant analysis (LDA; Duda et al., 2001).
evidence_reasoning: This describes the MVPA analysis method.

claim: If the neural activation patterns did not differ systematically between sequences, accuracy should be 25% (guessing rate).
source_text: If the neural activation patterns did not differ systematically between sequences, accuracy should be 25% (guessing rate).
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the expected chance performance for a 4-way classifier.

claim: Systematically higher classification rates indicate that a region showed differential activation patterns for the four sequences.
source_text: Systematically higher classification rates indicate that a region showed differential activation patterns for the four sequences
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of what above-chance classification means.

claim: The size of the classification accuracy served as a measure of the strength of the sequence representation in that region.
source_text: and the size of the classification accuracy served as a measure of the strength of the sequence representation in that region
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of what classification accuracy magnitude indicates.
